items.entity: tip load on the free (right) edge
items.description: Sec. 3.5 says only 'cantilever beam (tip load, fixed left edge)'. The tip is the free right edge, but where on that edge the load acts is not stated. The figures that would show it (Figs. 6–9) are not available.
readings: mid-height of the right edge (y = 0.5·H)
bottom-right corner (y = 0; 99-line/top88 cantilever convention)
top-right corner (y = H)

items.description: Sec. 3.5 does not say whether the tip load is one nodal force or is spread over several nodes or a segment of the right edge.
readings: single nodal point force
force spread over a few nodes (≈2–5) around the load point
uniform (or parabolic) shear traction over the whole right edge

items.description: 'Tip load' (Sec. 3.5) gives no direction. A transverse (vertical) force is the usual convention. Its sign does not affect compliance or layout in linear elasticity.
readings: vertical/transverse, downward (−y); sign immaterial for compliance and layout
horizontal/axial tip force (unconventional)

items.description: No force magnitude is given anywhere. The compliance values in Table 5 (≈76–81) suggest a normalized unit load with E0 = 1, but this is never stated.
readings: |F| = 1 (normalized)
a physical magnitude (e.g. 1 kN)

items.description: Sec. 3.5 gives only ν = 0.3 and the ratio Emin/E0 = 1e-9. The value of E0 itself is never stated.
readings: E0 = 1 (normalized), Emin = 1e-9
a physical modulus (e.g. 210 GPa or 70 GPa)

items.description: The paper does not say whether the 2-D problems are plane stress or plane strain. With ν = 0.3, plane strain is equivalent to plane stress with ν ≈ 0.43, which changes the element stiffness non-proportionally.
readings: plane stress (99-line/top88 element matrix)
plane strain

items.description: No thickness is given for the 2-D domain.
readings: t = 1 (unit thickness)
another thickness value

items.entity: design domain orientation, aspect ratio and physical size
items.description: Tables 4/5 give only '120×60' (elements). Nothing explicitly says that 120 runs along the beam axis (horizontal, away from the fixed left edge), that the elements are square, or what the physical L×H is. A 2:1 domain of unit square elements is implied only by convention.
readings: nelx = 120 along the beam axis × nely = 60 in height, unit square elements (L:H = 2:1)
same 2:1 domain at a physical scale (e.g. 2 × 1 with h = 1/60), rmin still counted in element widths
60 wide × 120 tall (reversed row/column convention)

items.description: The rmin values (fixed 1.5; Table 1 1.50→1.20; tail 1.20; range [1.1, 4.0]) are given without units, and Eq. 3 uses distances between element centroids. They only make sense in element widths, but the element size is never stated.
readings: rmin in element widths (h = 1): 1.5 → 3×3 stencil incl. diagonals, 1.2 → 5-point stencil
rmin in physical length units of a non-unit element size (changes the stencil)

items.description: Vf = 0.40 is stated (Sec. 3.5, Table 4), but not which field the volume constraint and the OC bisection act on, or whether it is an equality or a ≤ constraint. With β up to 32 and η = 0.5, the volumes of ρ, ρ̄ and ρ̃ differ substantially.
readings: on the physical (projected) density ρ̃
on the filtered density ρ̄
on the raw design variables ρ

items.entity: initial density field / role of random seeds
items.description: The starting density is never given. Sec. 4.5 ('tail starts from uniform density') and σ = 0.000 for the fixed and schedule-only controllers suggest a deterministic uniform start. But Sec. 1.2 speaks of runs 'perturbed by different random seeds', and Sec. 3.5 reports n = 5 'independent random seeds' without saying what is randomized.
readings: uniform ρ = Vf = 0.40 (seeds affect only LLM sampling)
uniform 0.40 plus a small seed-dependent random perturbation

items.description: Sec. 3.1 says only 'OC method with move limit δ'. The damping exponent, the Lagrange-multiplier bisection range and tolerance, whether δ is an absolute bound on the design variable, and the density bounds are not given.
readings: top88-style OC: damping exponent 0.5, absolute move ±δ, bisection on λ to relative tol 1e-3, ρ ∈ [0,1]
OC with a different damping exponent (e.g. 0.3) and/or a tighter bisection tolerance (e.g. 1e-6)
δ applied as a relative (proportional) move limit

items.description: Sec. 3.5 mentions no passive regions for the cantilever. Nothing says whether the whole 120×60 domain is designable or whether a solid pad sits under the point load.
readings: no passive elements (whole 120×60 domain designable)
small passive solid patch at the load application point

items.entity: best valid snapshot ρ* entering the 40-iteration tail
items.description: Sec. 3.5 defines ρ* as the field with the lowest compliance 'while satisfying the volume constraint'. The Table 7 footnote and Sec. 4.5 add a validity gate 'p ≥ 3.0 and G < 0.25', stated only for the 3-D and tail-only runs. The volume tolerance, whether compliances evaluated at different p/β are compared directly, and whether ρ, ρ̄ or ρ̃ is stored and reloaded for the tail are not stated.
readings: valid = volume constraint satisfied only; snapshot stores the raw design field ρ
valid = volume satisfied AND p ≥ 3.0 AND G < 0.25; snapshot stores ρ
same gate, but the snapshot stores and reloads the physical field ρ̃

items.description: Sec. 3.4 says the schedule-only controller executes the Table 1 stages. At N = 300 that means β 4→16 over it. 150–225 and β = 32 only from it. 225. But Sec. 4.3 says it 'commits to β = 32 by iteration 80', and the Fig. 9 caption says β ≥ 16 by iteration 80. The ramp shapes within stages are not stated, and Table 3 (PHASE.penal = 22, PHASE.sharp = 16, BETA_DOUBLE = 10) hints at phases counted in iterations instead.
readings: Table 1 budget fractions of N = 300: boundaries at it. 24/150/225, linear p ramps (1→2, 2→4.5), β 1→4→16 within stages 2–3, β = 32 from it. 225, rmin/δ stepped 1.50/0.20 → 1.35/0.15 → 1.25/0.08 → 1.20/0.05
iteration-count phases from Table 3 (Stage 2 = 22 its, Stage 3 = 16 its), so β = 32 is reached at ≈ it. 60–80
fallback-style ramp (p over 12 its, then β doubling every 10 its up to 32), reaching β = 32 by ≈ it. 60–80 as in Sec. 4.3

items.description: Sec. 3.4 says only: 'p ramps linearly from 1.0 to 4.5 over 30 iterations; β doubles every 10 iterations after the ramp; rmin is tightened in the late stage'. The initial β, the β cap, the start/end rmin and when it is tightened, δ, and any restart rule are not given.
readings: β = 1 doubling at it. 40, 50, … capped at 32; rmin 1.5 → 1.2 over the last ≈25% of N; δ = 0.2 constant
β capped at 64 (Table 2 upper bound); rmin 1.5 → 1.2; δ lowered to 0.05 late
rmin stepped 1.5 → 1.35 → 1.25 → 1.20 and δ 0.2 → 0.05 following the Table 1 stage values

items.description: Sec. 3.4 gives only 'step-wise p ramp (+0.75 per 10 iterations), β raised only once p ≥ 3.0, restart when C > 1.12·C*'. The starting and maximum p, the β increment rule/period/cap, the rmin and δ schedules, and what a restart reloads or resets are not given.
readings: p = 1.0 + 0.75 every 10 its capped at 4.5; β doubling every 10 its once p ≥ 3 (≈ it. 30) up to 32; rmin = 1.5, δ = 0.2 constant; restart reloads ρ* only
p starting at 1.5; β doubling every 20 its capped at 16–32; rmin/δ lowered to 1.2/0.05 late
β, rmin and δ following the Table 1 stage values once p ≥ 3; restart also resets p/β to the snapshot's values

items.entity: LLM agent controller (prompt, model, restart semantics)
items.description: The verbatim system prompt is withheld ('released upon publication'). The model is a preview build (gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview), and run-to-run σ = 0.021 shows the outputs are not deterministic. The parameters before the first call (it. 1–4) and what a restart resets (density only, or also p/β/rmin/δ) are not specified. Only the Table 1 scaffold, the Table 2 bounds and gate, k = 5 and temperature 0 are given.
readings: replay the Table 6 excerpt as a piecewise-constant schedule (k = 5) with restarts to ρ* at it. 165, 200, 225, 300
re-run an available LLM at temperature 0 with a prompt rebuilt from Tables 1–2 and the β ≤ 8 (G > 0.20) gate, k = 5
use the deterministic fallback ramp (Table 1 / Table 3 constants)

items.entity: LLM agent stage breakpoints and β/gate trace
items.description: Table 1 puts Sharpening at 50–75% and Converge at 75–100% of N (it. 150/225), but Table 6 uses 45–55% and 67–100% (it. 135/200). Sec. 4.2 says the gate was active at it. 85–134 with requested β advances 'silently capped', but Table 6 shows the gate off at it. 85 and β = 4, which a β ≤ 8 cap cannot produce. Sec. 4.1 and Fig. 8 put the G = 0.20 crossing at ≈ it. 150, while Table 6 shows the gate off from it. 135.
readings: Table 1 breakpoints (it. 24/150/225 at N = 300)
Table 6 breakpoints (≈ it. 24/135/200)
Table 6 β values taken literally (β = 4 until it. 135, 8 at 145, 16 at 155, 32 from ≈ it. 200)

items.description: Table 4 gives N = 300, but Fig. 1 says 'up to N main-loop iterations'. Sec. 5.3 mentions 'additional restart iterations' and a reduced 'effective run length' for an early-converged run. It is not stated whether there is an early-stop tolerance, or whether restarts consume or extend the 300-iteration budget.
readings: exactly 300 main-loop iterations; restarts consume budget
300 iterations plus extra iterations after each restart
early termination on an unstated convergence tolerance (e.g. max |Δρ| < 0.01)

items.entity: Heaviside projection in the fixed (no-continuation) controller
items.description: Sec. 3.4 says the fixed controller runs with constant p = 3, β = 1, rmin = 1.5, δ = 0.2. Eq. 4 at β = 1 is only 'nearly linear', so it is unclear whether the projection is applied or bypassed (ρ̃ = ρ̄).
readings: apply Eq. 4 with β = 1, η = 0.5
bypass the projection: ρ̃ = ρ̄ (standard density-filtered SIMP)

items.entity: finite element type for the 120×60 grid
items.description: The 2-D element formulation is never stated; Sec. 3.5 only mentions direct sparse factorization (SciPy). The paper's only DOF count (≈110,000 DOFs for the 40×20×10 3-D mesh, Sec. 5.3) does not match trilinear 8-node hexahedra (≈28,400 DOFs), so linear elements cannot be taken for granted.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilateral (Q4), 2×2 Gauss integration (99-line/top88 element)
8-node serendipity quadrilateral (Q8)
